summary.headline: Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels FY26 consolidated revenue rose 12% to INR 707 crore, with PAT of INR 66 crore; Q4 revenue up 4% to INR 184 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated operating revenue was INR 184 crore (up 4% YoY), with EBITDA of INR 53 crore (28.85% margin) and PAT of INR 12 crore (6.44% margin). Management blamed Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad on the Middle East war, saying occupancy there has recovered to over 90%. For FY26, revenue grew 12%, EBITDA was INR 218 crore (30.82% margin) and PAT was INR 66 crore (9.21% margin), with profitability hit by the Middle East war and higher depreciation and finance costs. Management reiterated the plan to double hotels to 85 and keys to 6,635 over four years, and said the EM Bypass Kolkata apartment sales are ahead of plan on cash flow.

financial_highlights.change: resilient despite high base; YoY not stated
ARR up 9% YoY; RevPAR up 7% YoY

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Park Calcutta ran at 100% occupancy for Q4 and FY26; Park Chennai (95%) and Park Navi Mumbai (93%) were the other top-three occupancies. Delhi and Hyderabad saw large Q4 cancellations, now recovered to over 90% occupancy.

segments.name: Flurys (F&B retail)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 29% YoY and the brand has 110 outlets. Management said it is profitable but did not share segment EBITDA. Plans to add 30+ outlets in 10 months (NCR 8, Pune 5, Bangalore 4).

segments.name: F&B overall
segments.commentary: F&B revenue crossed INR 300 crore in FY26, about 43% of total revenue.

segments.name: Real estate (EM Bypass Kolkata)
segments.commentary: 29 of 34 apartments sold in the first block at an average INR 20,857 per sq ft. Cash flow improved by over INR 11 crore up to April 2026, with a further ~INR 70 crore expected this year; second block launch planned for Sep-Oct 2026.

guidance_outlook: Reach over 3,000 keys by FY27 after adding 12 hotels (472 keys), of which 8 are asset-light.
Over four years: hotels from 42 to 85, keys from 2,677 to 6,635; owned hotels to double, asset-light to triple.
Flurys to reach 140 outlets (or slightly more) after 30 additions in 10 months, and 40-50 more outlets by 2030.
Park Mumbai Juhu (78 rooms) construction to start June 2026, completion by about March 2027.
Malabar House (Cochin) acquisition expected to close in June 2026; Vizag (100 rooms) moved to early 2030 opening due to environmental clearance delays.
Interest cost at about 8.35% (MCLR), expected to stay below that level; capex and acquisition needs of about INR 1,500 crore over five years, mainly funded by internal accruals.
Management said earlier mid-teens top-line growth guidance was missed; FY26 came in at 12%.
capex_capacity: Five projects (Pune, Mumbai, Vizag, EM Bypass, Jaipur) totalling 950 rooms at about INR 1.2 crore per room, about INR 1,100 crore before the EM Bypass reduction.
EM Bypass expected to contribute INR 350 crore, of which INR 70 crore is expected this year.
Zillion and THALI acquisition/project cost about INR 330 crore; normal capex about INR 40 crore per year; Flurys capex about INR 30-40 crore per year.
Q4 FY26 launches: Zone by the Park Darjeeling, Zone Connect by the Park Gangtok and Zone Connect by the Park Katra; 7 properties (283 keys) launched in FY26.
Flurys moving from central kitchen to an outsourced manufacturing vendor (agreement signed).
Room renovations planned at Chennai, Bangalore, Kolkata and Vizag; 20 rooms at Park Calcutta to be refurbished.
demand_pricing: Management cited limited branded supply in India (about 216,000 rooms) and said supply growth is 200-300 bps below demand growth.
Kolkata has 5,101 keys with about 1,702 keys expected over five years; management said the outlook is positive, helped by the change of state government.

Ran Baas The Palace (Patiala, leased) ran at ARR of about INR 31,000 in FY26; Lotus Palace Chettinad at about INR 12,000 ARR and about 30% occupancy; Patiala targets about 50% occupancy in the Oct-Dec season.
Cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad in Q4 due to the Middle East war; management said contracts with ministries and corporates have been re-established.
Park Calcutta has about 30% repeat customers and T-RevPAR near INR 24,000, which management said is above luxury peers in its CBD.
Management said the Operation Sindoor disruption hit Q1 FY26 and the Middle East war hit from late February into April 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ADR decline sequentially and grow only 3% YoY in Q4, and why was FY26 growth 12% against a mid-teens expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 weakness to large cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad from the Middle East war, which have since stabilised. It said 12% growth was good given two disruptions (Operation Sindoor in Q1 and the Middle East war).

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Flurys outlet count below earlier guidance, and what is the achievable expansion plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan is 30+ outlets in the next 10 months (from 110 to about 140), largely cafes, with flagships in each new market; 40-50 more outlets by 2030. Management said the asset-light model with outsourced production allows faster rollout.

qa_highlights.question: How is 100% occupancy at Park Calcutta calculated when the website shows rooms available?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 100% means all rooms occupied every day, that the hotel has delivered near-100% occupancy for about 10 years (excluding COVID), and that its revenue management and repeat base (about 30%) drive this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kolkata outlook and how is the EM Bypass sales progress?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Kolkata supply is limited and the state government change is positive. Apartments were launched at about INR 18,225 per sq ft and are now selling near INR 21,000; second block expected around the festive season.

qa_highlights.question: How will Flurys maintain quality with the central kitchen dropped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the central kitchen plan was dropped in favour of an outsourced vendor, with recipe standardisation, quality checks and quality chefs on site at the production facility.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company keep interest costs under control during the capex cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Atul Khosla said the interest rate is about 8.35% (MCLR) and will stay below that. Capex of about INR 1,500 crore over five years is mostly funded by internal accruals, with about INR 80 crore cash on hand; project interest will be capitalised as IDC.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the Vizag delay to 2030 and the status of Malabar House?
qa_highlights.answer: Vizag was delayed by environmental clearance, which is now in place; the project has no basement, so it may be faster, but management kept a 2030 timeline. Malabar House acquisition is expected to close in June 2026 after bank approval for foreign payment.

risks_watch: Q4 cancellations in Delhi and Hyderabad and whether occupancy holds above 90% in the coming quarters.
Geopolitical and LPG supply disruption, and its effect on costs and travel demand.
Flurys execution: 30 outlet additions in 10 months and the shift to outsourced production.
Vizag delay to 2030 and dependence on government permissions for new projects.
Pace of EM Bypass second-block launch (Sep-Oct 2026) and about INR 70 crore cash inflow expected this year.
Blended ARR and occupancy for the 336 leased keys not disclosed on the call; to be emailed to an analyst.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, pricing and the long-term pipeline, while being defensive on the FY26 growth miss and Q4 cancellations. Management was evasive on segment EBITDA (Flurys) and on the leased-hotel blended metrics, and on the Calcutta 100% occupancy calculation.

The sale of service apartments at EM Bypass Kolkata has exceeded expectations, resulting in substantial improvement in this year's cash flow.
So this year because of Operation Sindoor, the quarter was not very strong but now with things stabilizing we expect this quarter to be a good quarter and a stable quarter.
We do not share the segment analysis but Flurys is a profitable business.
